Figure 5: Final feature-set. All-pair Correlation-Heatmap for S_2648 training instances. DDG refers to experimental DDG labels. A, B, C, D, and E, are our proposed PMPNN extracted features, while F, G, and H are widely used evolutionary features. It can be observed that among A, B, C, and D, all pairs seem sufficiently uncorrelated. On the other hand, feature C shows a PCC of -0.15 with the corresponding experimental DDG values, which is the minimum feature-label correlation in terms of PCC magnitude. Thus, the features are individually potent for the task of experimental DDG prediction due to satisfactory feature-label correlation, and they might perform well together due to low feature-feature correlations. Additionally, F, G, and H show maximum PCC magnitudes of 0.32, 0.15, and 0.39 with A, A, and E-1, respectively. This indicates that most of the dimensions in our final feature space contain significantly non-overlapping information encoding different aspects of the mutation under consideration.
